annotations.text:
BRIGHTCV — one complete design.

PALETTE (no white, no blue): warm sand #EBD9BB page, cream card #FBF3E3, chocolate #3A2A1E chrome, ink #2A1D14. Four working colours — rust #C1442A (do this now), marigold #F2A81D (in progress, XP), moss #4E7A34 (done), berry #A02454 (rewards).

TYPE: Tinos throughout — metrically identical to Times New Roman, so it falls back to real Times with no shift.

WHY IT DOESN'T READ AS AI: no gradients anywhere, no soft blurred shadows, no emoji. Flat colour blocks, 2px ink outlines, hard offset shadows, and a halftone dot ground — the vocabulary of printed board games and letterpress, not of a component library.

THE GAME LAYER — earned, not sprinkled.

XP is only ever awarded for a change that measurably improves the CV: an achievement line containing a number (+20), a summary trimmed under 60 words (+25), a finished stage (+40). Nothing is given for logging in, and there is no leaderboard — ranking job-hunters against each other would be cruel.

The six builder sections become six STAGES with XP values. The dashboard's five-step journey (Drafted, Filled in, Polishing, ATS 80+, Sent out) is drawn from data the app already has: completion, ATS score, exports.

Levels unlock templates. Badges name real accomplishments. And the whole layer switches off in Account — see the note on the Rewards screen.

PHONES · 390×844 — the CV in the preview stays plain white and print-safe no matter what the app is wearing, which is both the existing constraint in the code and a nice contrast against the colour. Every target is 44px or larger; no fake status bar, since the real one draws over it.
